title: Unified Inference: Product PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing (v2)
author: Ava Thompson
body:
Overview

This document aggregates the end-to-end product specification for the next major release of Unified Inference (v2). It contains: product overview and goals, prioritized PRD requirements, high-level design specifications, roadmap and themes for the next three quarters, pricing and packaging notes, and release notes and rollout guidance. The audience includes product, engineering, solutions, and go-to-market teams.

1) Product overview and goals

- Product name: Unified Inference — v2
- Vision: Provide a single, consistent inference API and operational experience across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments while improving per-token unit economics and reducing 95th percentile latency for synchronous generation.
- Target customers: AI-native startups, mid-market & enterprise product teams, platform teams requiring standardization.

Goals (measured):
- Improve hosted API p95 token-generation latency by 20% for typical 512-token workloads (baseline: 180ms -> target: <=145ms).
- Reduce average per-token cost by 15% via batching, caching, and quantization recommendations in Redwood Optimize.
- Deliver a first-class Dedicated rollout experience (canary + automated rollback) with SLA-ready observability.
- Ship pricing & packaging options that increase attach rate for Redwood Optimize by +10% in Q1 post-launch.

2) Product requirements (PRD) — prioritized

A. Core API and UX (MUST):
- Expose unified /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints with identical semantics across deployment modes.
- Streaming support and function/tool-calling available in hosted and dedicated at GA.
- Model pinning and versioning for customers (per-route).
- Token-level billing export and per-route cost estimates in the Console.

B. Performance & Reliability (MUST):
- p95 latency SLO for hosted generation: <=150ms (512 tokens, base-cases).
- Platform-wide availability target: 99.95% for hosted API.
- Auto-fallback policy: route to compatible model variant (quantized/FP16) when primary model capacity is constrained.

C. Cost Controls (SHOULD):
- Intelligent batching suggestion engine in Redwood Optimize (suggested batch sizes, TTLs).
- Automatic prefix/KV cache re-use for repeated prompt prefixes.
- Quantization profile recommendations for customer workloads (safe/regression-tested).

D. Dedicated & Private (SHOULD/COULD):
- Dedicated autoscaling policies with reserved and burst capacity knobs.
- Private control plane option (VPC) with KMS integration for key management.

E. Observability & Rollouts (MUST):
- Per-model route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, trace sampling hooks.
- Canary and A/B rollout pipelines with automatic rollback on defined quality regressions.

Non-functional constraints:
- Backwards compatibility: v1 API compatibility matrix required for third-party SDKs.
- Security: All hosted traffic must support customer-managed keys for enterprise customers and satisfy SOC2 controls.

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- Baseline perf tests run with benchmark suite: improvement in p95 by >=20% across target workloads.
- Pricing calculator updated and validated with finance; new packaging published in Console.
- Integration tests for dedicated autoscale and private VPC onboarding pass in staging.

3) Design specs — high level

Architecture overview
- Serving runtime: GPU-optimized inference engine with kernel selection layer, KV cache manager, and batching scheduler.
- Control plane: model registry, route config, rollout engine, observability ingestion.
- Data plane: request routing, model host pools, fallback router.

Key components and responsibilities
- API Gateway (team: eng-platform): validate requests, enforce quotas, authenticate.
- Router (team: eng-serving-runtime): policy-based routing (latency/cost/region), fallback logic.
- Runtime Hosts (team: eng-serving-runtime): optimized kernels, quantization-aware execution, continuous batching.
- Optimize Service (team: eng-app-ml): generate batching/quantization suggestions and maintain per-customer profiles.
- Console (team: eng-developer-experience): per-route dashboards, pricing calculator, rollout UI.

API contracts (example)
- POST /v1/generate (JSON body)

Example request:
{
  "model": "unified-v2-1",
  "input": "Summarize the following text...",
  "max_tokens": 512,
  "stream": false,
  "route_config": { "pin": "v2.1", "fallback": "auto" }
}

Response (success) contains: request_id, model_version, tokens, timing_breakdown (decode_ms, kernel_ms).

Design decisions and tradeoffs
- Continuous batching vs. strict per-request latency: we bias to preserve p95 latency SLO (bound batch waiting time to 10ms) and accept slightly suboptimal batch fill rates.
- Quantization recommendations will be conservative for high-regulation customers; a regression-testing harness will gate profile suggestions.

Operational controls & SLOs
- Latency SLOs: hosted p95 <= 150ms; dedicated SLA set per-customer contract (example: 99.9% uptime, p95 <= 120ms on reserved capacity).
- Error budget: 1% monthly error budget for critical endpoints; automatic alerts when burn rate > 2x.

4) Roadmap & themes (next 3 quarters)

Q4 2026 (January–March) — Launch preparation
- Stabilize v2 runtime performance and complete benchmarking suite run.
- Redwood Optimize integration: batching suggestion MVP and quantization profile alpha.
- Pricing & packaging proposal finalized with finance; early access for key customers.

Q1 2027 (April–June) — GA and growth
- GA for hosted v2 with streaming and function-calls.
- Dedicated on-boarding flow: reserved capacity + autoscaling policies.
- Console rollout: per-route cost insights and automated recommendations.

Q2 2027 (July–September) — Expansion & enterprise readiness
- Private deployment packaging (VPC) with KMS support and compliance checklist.
- Advanced rollout features: A/B experiments, quality-metric-driven traffic shifts.
- Pricing refresh based on first-quarter usage telemetry.

Cross-cutting themes:
- Performance-first: Kernels and scheduling optimizations prioritized.
- Cost-aware controls: product features that let customers trade latency vs cost.
- Operationalization: make rollouts and migrations low-friction for customers.

5) Pricing & packaging notes

Proposed tiers (summary)
- Developer (self-serve): pay-as-you-go hosted API, per-token pricing baseline, streaming included, rate limits 60 RPM.
- Business (mid-market): committed usage discounts (monthly commit), access to Redwood Optimize suggestions, higher rate limits, support SLA (24h).
- Enterprise (reserved & private): reserved capacity contracts, custom pricing, private deployments, compliance add-ons, 4h support SLA.

Packaging details:
- Redwood Optimize add-on: priced as % of monthly usage savings (metered) or flat per-node fee for dedicated customers.
- Dedicated: commit tiers (S, M, L) with burst capacity add-on. Example: S = 1 GPU pool equivalent, M = 4, L = 16.
- Private: platform fee + per-node license + optional support. KMS and longer log retention are billed as add-ons.

Pricing examples (illustrative):
- Developer: $0.0009 / token (generation); $0.0003 / token (embedding).
- Business: 15% discount on usage with minimum monthly commit $10k; Optimize add-on $1k/mo or 10% of realized savings.
- Enterprise: custom list; expected effective per-token 30–60% lower than Developer for large commits.

Migration & incentives:
- Pilot credits for first three months for Business customers adopting v2.
- Free Optimize trial for 30 days.

6) Release notes — v2 (high level)

Release: Unified Inference v2.0 — 2026-11-15
Highlights:
- Unified API parity across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- p95 latency improvement of ~20% on benchmark suite.
- Streaming and function-calling GA for hosted and dedicated.
- Redwood Optimize batching suggestions (MVP) and quantization profile alpha.
- Console: per-route cost estimates and rollout UI for canary/A-B tests.

Breaking changes / migration notes:
- Model version pinning semantics tightened: customers using edge-case aliasing must migrate to explicit model_version in their routes. Migration tooling and scripts provided in the repo and Console.
- Billing export column changes: timing_breakdown fields added (decode_ms, kernel_ms) — update ingestion scripts.

Rollout plan
- Week 0: Staged rollout to internal customers and heavy-traffic partner accounts (feature flags on).
- Week 1–2: Open beta to Developer and Business tiers; monitor p95 and error budget.
- Week 3–6: GA for all hosted customers; dedicated and private onboarding by request.
- Rollback plan: Automated global rollback to v1 model variants + traffic shift if key quality/regression signals exceed thresholds.

Monitoring & success metrics
- Primary: p95 latency, monthly active routes, Redwood Optimize attach rate, per-token revenue.
- Secondary: Dedicated onboarding time (days), private deployment checklist passes, number of pricing migrations.

7) Ownership and next steps

- Product owner: Ava Thompson (product) — responsible for roadmap, PRD signoffs, pricing decisions.
- Eng leads: Mateo Ruiz (serving-runtime), Linh Tran (platform), Naomi Green (devex/console).
- Go-to-market: Michael Chen — launch plan, enablement, case studies.

Immediate next steps (action items):
1. Engineering: finalize benchmarking suite and perf targets (owner: Mateo) — due 2026-11-22.
2. Finance: finalize pricing model and draft contractual language for Dedicated/Private (owner: Priya Nair) — due 2026-11-29.
3. DevEx: Console UX for pricing calculator and rollout UI (owner: Naomi) — due 2026-12-06.
4. Sales/SE: recruit 3 pilot customers for early access program (owner: Michael Chen) — due 2026-11-30.
